speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Health in view of the proposed increases in premiums and coverage of MediShield Life (MSHL), whether MediSave withdrawal limits for MSHL premium payments will be raised so that MediSave can be used to fully pay for premiums for MediShield Life Basic, Integrated Shield Plans for Class B2/C wards and the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (for public hospital Class B1 coverage), for all age groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: As MediShield Life already provides universal and basic insurance coverage for all Singaporeans, policyholders will need to consider whether they need the additional IP insurance and the affordability of the IP premiums when choosing these plans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: First, with the proposed increased coverage of MediShield Life, does this reduce the burden on the lower tier Integrated Shield Plans and, hence, translate to lower premiums for the IPs?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Second, according a comparison of standard IPs for Class B1 coverage on the MOH website, the benefits of standard IPs are identical across all IP insurers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This being the case, has the Government considered having CPF take over the running of standard IPs for Class B1 coverage so that the costs and premiums can be kept lower?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: By having CPF take over the standard IP, risks can be further pooled rather than split across different insurers and the premiums can be possibly lowered.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Now, the proposal is to increase the coverage or MediShield Life.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Would that eat into some of the Integrated Shield Plan coverage such that the premiums of Integrated Shield Plans can be lowered?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: With regard to the second question which the Senior Minister of State answered, he mentioned that B1 plans are the icing on the cake.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But I understand that the B1 plans are actually quite popular among Singaporeans, to the extent that the Government has gone to the extent of standardising the benefits of all the B1 plans so that there is not so much need for comparison for premium holders.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, the question is: can that, therefore, be brought under the CPF fold so that we can possibly benefit from risk-pooling and, possibly, lower premiums for premium holders?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is an on-going process of reviewing the utilisation over time and we may evolve some of this coverage over time as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, this thing will take some time to settle.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Nonetheless. we will take the suggestion into consideration The increased coverage for MediShield Life, the expansion of increased coverage up to about 120,000 claims per year, actually, that refers to total bill size.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That does not necessarily mean, therefore, that the need for private plan is negated by the increased coverage, because there is still healthcare inflation and choosing private coverage is actually a matter of personal choice.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some people prefer to go to the private sector where they can have, perhaps, a more personalised type of higher value service.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But those who are looking for good value care will still come back to the institution in our restructured hospitals.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I do not think those two are mutually inclusive and increasing coverage for one would necessarily eat into the other.
